chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad all together, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who pilfered a garment from the market. So they said, 'This man has stolen.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'I do not cut [the hand] for the open theft (al-daghara), but I cut the hand of the one who takes and then hides.'

key_terms.الدَّغَارَةِ: Open theft or picking up belongings openly
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: To cut (referring to amputation of the hand as punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between open theft and hidden theft in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between 'open theft' (daghara), where the hand is not cut, and 'hidden theft', where the hand is cut, establishing a nuance in the application of the hadd penalty based on the manner of taking the property. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the thief's intent and the visibility of the act, contrasting with broader interpretations that focus solely on the value of stolen goods. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt in applying hadd punishments with precision and mercy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad altogether, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws judged regarding a man who pilferred clothes from the market. So they said, ‘This man has stolen’. So heasws said, ‘Iasws do not cut with regardsin the Al-Dagara (picking up somebody else’s belongings) openly, but Iasws cut a hand of the one who takes, then hides’.
